To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FGF signalling is important for the normal development of the zebrafish telencephalon, diencephalon and midline, and that FGFs have unique and combinated roles during forebrain development.

fgf3 and/or fgf8 are required for the formation and/or patterning of all major forebrain subdivisions, and that fgf3 alone is required to specify telencephalic identity, and for the development of the ZLI and optic stalk.
Fgf3 and/or Fgf8 are required to specify the telencephalon and ventral thalamocaudal diencephalon.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms underlying the patterning of the zebrafish brain.
the mechanisms that regulate the development of the vertebrate forebrain, which includes the telencephalon, diencephalon and midbrain.
the roles of FGF signalling in patterning and development of the forebrain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two factors have distinct functions in the forebrain, but also have some overlapping roles.
Fgf8 is required for the development of the forebrain and Fgf3 is required for the formation of the forebrain.
Fgf3 and 8 have unique and combinating roles during forebrain development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Fgf3 and/or Fgf8 are essential for the normal development of all forebrain regions.

Fgf8 has a role in patterning of the midline and ZLI and is required for the normal formation of the forebrain commissures, while Fgf3 is required for normal expression of telencephalon markers and patterning of the ventral thalamic region.
Fgf3 and/or Fgf8 are involved in patterning and/or formation of most regions of the forebrain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FGF signalling has a critical role during zebrafishtelecephalon development and that the FGF ligands Fgf3 and fgf 8 have unique and combi natorial roles in this process.
